ropriations Act, 2016

This bill provides continuing FY2016 appropriations to federal agencies through December 11, 2015, or until the enactment of the applicable appropriations legislation.

It prevents a government shutdown that would otherwise occur when the existing FY2015 appropriations expire on September 30, 2015.

The bill includes provisions that:

- Extend the authority for the Department of Health and Human Services to make payments from the Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund and the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund for services provided to individuals enrolled in Medicare.
- Extend the authority for the Department of Veterans Affairs to continue certain health care services.
- Extend the authority for the Department of Transportation to make expenditures from the Highway Trust Fund.
- Extend the authority for the Department of Homeland Security to obligate funds for the National Flood Insurance Program.
- Extend the authority for the Department of Agriculture to continue certain nutrition assistance programs.

The bill also includes provisions related to the Overseas Contingency Operations/Global War on Terrorism.

It prohibits any funding provided by this bill from being used to initiate or resume any project or activity for which funds were not available during FY2015.

The bill is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010.

DescriptionTrim: To revise the national flood insurance program to provide for mitigation of potential flood damages and management of coastal erosion,
Description: ensure the financial soundness of the program, and increase compliance with the mandatory purchase requirement, and for other purposes.
DescriptionLLM: to improve the mapping of flood hazards, to provide for the affordability of flood insurance, and for other purposes. This bill aims to enhance the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) by incorporating measures for better flood risk assessment, encouraging the use of advanced technologies in flood mapping, and promoting community resilience through grants and incentives for flood mitigation projects. Additionally, it seeks to address the financial stability of the NFIP by adjusting premium rates to reflect true risk levels while ensuring affordability for low-income policyholders. The bill also includes provisions for the management and reduction of coastal erosion through coordinated efforts with state and local governments.
